tracks.name: Figure
tracks.blurb: Movement, structure and proportion of the whole body.

units.title: Gesture
units.goal: Catch the movement of a pose before any detail. A gesture is a few lines that show where the weight goes and how the body bends.
look: One long line from the head through the body to the foot that carries the weight
Shoulders and hips usually tilt in opposite directions
When the time is up, stop, even mid-line

ex.title: 20 poses, 30 seconds each
ex.how: Only the line of action and the tilt of shoulders and hips.

ex.title: 10 poses, 1 minute each
ex.how: Add the head and the limbs as single lines.

ex.title: 5 poses, 2 minutes each
ex.how: Put the rib cage and pelvis on top of the gesture as two simple masses.

units.title: Structure
units.goal: Turn the gesture into simple forms that sit in space: boxes for the chest and pelvis, cylinders for the limbs.
look: Draw through the forms, including the edges you can't see
Where one form overlaps another, show it with the line
Ellipses at the joints show which way a limb points

ex.title: 8 poses, 2 minutes each
ex.how: Chest and pelvis as boxes. Show how they tilt and turn against each other.

ex.title: 6 views from above and below, 3 minutes each
ex.how: Limbs as cylinders. Overlaps tell what's in front.

ex.title: Five poses from memory
ex.how: Without a reference, draw five mannequin poses you remember from today.

units.title: Proportion
units.goal: Measure and check. Compare lengths against the head and the torso, then check your drawing on top of the reference.
look: Find the halfway point of the figure: usually around the hips
Compare one length with another before you commit
Look at the negative shapes between arms and body

ex.title: Draw one pose, then compare
ex.how: Draw a pose for 15 minutes, photograph it and lay it over the reference in Compare.

ex.title: 4 foreshortened poses, 5 minutes each
ex.how: Measure with your pencil at arm's length.

ex.title: A foreshortened pose, checked
ex.how: Draw for 20 minutes, then check the proportions in Compare.

units.title: Master figure drawings
units.goal: Copy drawings by artists who solved these problems before you, and notice their choices.
look: Where did the artist simplify, and where did they add detail?
Which lines are dark and which are light?
Copy the proportions first, the shading last

ex.title: 6 drawings, 2 minutes each
ex.how: A quick gesture over each master drawing.

ex.title: One copy, 30 minutes
ex.how: Pick one drawing and copy it carefully.

ex.title: Copy and compare
ex.how: Copy a drawing for 30 minutes, then lay your copy over it in Compare.

tracks.name: Heads
tracks.blurb: The head as a form you can turn in any direction, then light and likeness.

units.title: Ball and plane
units.goal: Build the head from a ball with flat sides and a jaw. The construction lines show which way the head faces.
look: The center line shows the turn; the brow line shows the tilt
The side of the head is flat, like a slice cut off a ball
The face divides into thirds: hairline to brow, brow to nose, nose to chin

ex.title: 10 heads, 1 minute each
ex.how: Only the ball, the side plane and the center line.

ex.title: 6 heads, 3 minutes each
ex.how: Add the brow line, the jaw and the thirds of the face.

ex.title: Ten heads from imagination
ex.how: Draw the ball and plane head in ten different directions without a reference.

units.title: Tilts and turns
units.goal: Read the angle of a head at a glance, without construction lines to help.
look: Find the center line of the face first
A head tilted up shows more of the jaw; tilted down, more of the top
The far eye and cheek get narrower as the head turns

ex.title: 15 heads, 30 seconds each
ex.how: Only the center line and the brow line.

ex.title: 8 heads, 2 minutes each
ex.how: Full construction on each head.

ex.title: One head, checked
ex.how: Draw one head for 15 minutes, then check it in Compare.

units.title: Light on the head
units.goal: See the head as light and shadow shapes. Group the shadows into one flat tone first.
look: Find the line where light turns into shadow
Keep everything in shadow one value until the end
The eye sockets and under the nose are the first places to go dark

ex.title: 6 heads, 3 minutes each
ex.how: Fill the shadow shape with one flat tone.

ex.title: Three values, then draw
ex.how: In the Studio set Values to 3, study the shapes, then draw for 20 minutes.

ex.title: One lit head, 25 minutes
ex.how: A full value study of one head.

units.title: Portrait studies
units.goal: Use what you know about the form of the head on real faces by master artists.
look: Construction first, features last
Features sit on the form; they turn with it
Look for the big shadow shapes before the details

ex.title: 8 heads, 2 minutes each
ex.how: Ball, plane and the thirds on each one.

ex.title: One copy, 30 minutes
ex.how: Copy a head carefully.

ex.title: Copy and compare
ex.how: Copy a head, then check it in Compare.

tracks.name: Perspective
tracks.blurb: Draw things so they sit convincingly in space.

units.title: Boxes
units.goal: Find the horizon and the vanishing points, then draw boxes through, including the hidden edges.
look: The horizon is at your eye level
Parallel edges meet at the same vanishing point
Vertical edges stay vertical in one and two point

ex.title: 12 scenes, 1 minute each
ex.how: Mark the horizon and vanishing points only.

ex.title: 6 scenes, 3 minutes each
ex.how: Draw each box through, with the hidden edges.

ex.title: A page of boxes
ex.how: Fill a page with boxes from imagination in two point perspective.

units.title: Cylinders and ellipses
units.goal: Draw round forms in space. Ellipses get rounder the further they are from your eye level.
look: The short axis of an ellipse follows the center line of the cylinder
Ellipses near the horizon are thin
Ellipses have no points at the ends

ex.title: 10 scenes, 1 minute each
ex.how: Center lines and ellipses only.

ex.title: 6 scenes, 3 minutes each
ex.how: Full cylinders, drawn through.

ex.title: Ellipse drill
ex.how: Three rows of ellipses, each row thinner. Draw from the shoulder.

units.title: Rooms and streets
units.goal: Put whole spaces together: walls, floors and objects that share the same vanishing points.
look: Start with the horizon and the biggest planes
Doors and windows share the wall's vanishing point
Repeat elements get smaller toward the vanishing point

ex.title: 6 scenes, 2 minutes each
ex.how: Horizon, vanishing points and the biggest planes.

ex.title: 3 scenes, 10 minutes each
ex.how: A full line drawing of each space.

ex.title: One scene, checked
ex.how: Draw a scene for 20 minutes, then check it in Compare.

units.title: Real places
units.goal: Find perspective in real streets, where nothing is perfectly lined up.
look: Find the horizon first, even if it's hidden behind buildings
Not every building faces the same way
Simplify: big boxes first, windows last

ex.title: 6 places, 2 minutes each
ex.how: Horizon and the main boxes of each street. Uses your Places board.

ex.title: 2 places, 15 minutes each
ex.how: A full drawing of one street.

ex.title: Invent a street
ex.how: Use what you drew to design a street of your own.

tracks.name: Light & value
tracks.blurb: How light falls on form, and how to group what you see into a few values.

units.title: Light on simple forms
units.goal: Learn the parts of light and shadow on simple forms you can see clearly.
look: Light, core shadow, reflected light and cast shadow
The core shadow is where the form turns away from the light
Cast shadows are darkest where they touch the object

ex.title: 10 forms, 1 minute each
ex.how: Draw only the shape of the shadow.

ex.title: 6 forms, 5 minutes each
ex.how: Show light, core shadow, reflected light and cast shadow.

units.title: Three values
units.goal: Simplify what you see into three values: light, middle and dark.
look: Squint to see the big shapes
A dark object in light can be the same value as a light object in shadow
Decide the value groups before you draw

ex.title: Three values in the Studio
ex.how: Set Values to 3, study the shapes, then draw them flat.

ex.title: 6 still lifes, 3 minutes each
ex.how: Three flat values, no blending.

ex.title: 6 master drawings, 3 minutes each
ex.how: Find the three value groups in each one.

units.title: Full range
units.goal: Go from three values to a full range, while keeping the big groups intact.
look: Lay in the three groups first
Add variation inside each group, not across them
Keep the lightest lights and darkest darks small

ex.title: One still life, 30 minutes
ex.how: A full value drawing.

ex.title: One master copy, 30 minutes
ex.how: Copy a value drawing.

ex.title: Draw, then compare
ex.how: A 30-minute value drawing, checked in Compare with Pencil view.

units.title: Master value studies
units.goal: Copy masters of tone and see how few values they really used.
look: Count the values: often there are fewer than you think
Notice where edges are soft and where they're hard
Squint at your copy and the original side by side

ex.title: One copy, 45 minutes
ex.how: A careful copy of a value drawing.

ex.title: Copy and compare
ex.how: Copy for 45 minutes, then lay your copy over it.

tracks.name: Color & light
tracks.blurb: Color temperature, value in color, and color from the masters.

units.title: Warm light, cool shadow
units.goal: See color temperature: warm light usually comes with cool shadows, and the other way round.
look: Compare the light side and the shadow side of the same object
Cast shadows pick up color from the sky or the room
Keep the values right even when the color changes

ex.title: 6 scenes, 5 minutes each
ex.how: Two colors only: one for the light, one for the shadow.

ex.title: One scene, 20 minutes
ex.how: A full color study.

units.title: Value first
units.goal: Color works when the values work. Check every color study in grayscale.
look: A bright color can be a dark value
Press G in the viewer to check values while you paint
If the gray version reads, the color version will too

ex.title: 6 paintings, 3 minutes each
ex.how: A grayscale study of each one first.

ex.title: Same painting in color
ex.how: Paint one in color, then compare both in grayscale.

units.title: Landscape color
units.goal: Use the light of the sky and the air between you and the distance.
look: Distant things get lighter, cooler and less contrasty
The sky is usually the lightest value
Shadows in daylight are often blue

ex.title: 6 landscapes, 5 minutes each
ex.how: Small color studies of the big shapes.

ex.title: One landscape, 30 minutes
ex.how: A color copy.

units.title: Master color copies
units.goal: Copy a painting to learn how its colors were mixed and placed.
look: Start with the big color shapes
Compare each color with its neighbors, not with the tube
Notice which colors repeat across the picture

ex.title: One copy, 45 minutes
ex.how: A color copy of a still life or interior.

ex.title: Copy and compare
ex.how: Copy a landscape, then check it in Compare.

tracks.name: Composition
tracks.blurb: Arranging shapes and values into pictures.

units.title: Thumbnails
units.goal: Small, quick drawings of a whole picture: the arrangement of big shapes, not the details.
look: Draw the frame first, small
Three to five shapes are enough
Notice where your eye goes first

ex.title: 10 paintings, 2 minutes each
ex.how: A thumbnail of the big shapes.

ex.title: 5 paintings, 5 minutes each
ex.how: Thumbnails with three values.

units.title: Light and dark pattern
units.goal: Reduce a picture to two values to see its pattern of light and dark.
look: Every shape is either light or dark
Strong pictures read at the size of a stamp
Connected darks make bigger, simpler shapes

ex.title: Two values in the Studio
ex.how: Set Values to 2, then thumbnail the pattern.

ex.title: 8 landscapes, 2 minutes each
ex.how: Two-value thumbnails.

units.title: Find the crop
units.goal: The same scene can make very different pictures. Try crops and guides to find the strongest one.
look: Try a tall and a wide crop of the same scene
Place the main shapes on a guide, then break the rule and compare
Leave room in the direction things face or move

ex.title: Three crops, one drawing
ex.how: Try three crops with different guides, fix the best one and draw it.

ex.title: Recompose a painting
ex.how: Find a new picture inside a painting and draw it.

units.title: Film frames
units.goal: Film directors compose every frame. Study how they place people, light and depth.
look: Where is the main subject in the frame?
How do lines in the set lead your eye?
What is in the dark?

ex.title: 8 frames, 2 minutes each
ex.how: Thumbnails of film frames. Uses your Film scenes board.

ex.title: Design your own frame
ex.how: Three thumbnails of a scene of your own, then one finished drawing.

units.title: Animal gesture
units.goal: Catch the movement of an animal the same way as a person: line of action first.
look: Find the spine first
Four legs: notice which carry the weight
Heads are often lower than you think

ex.title: 15 animals, 45 seconds each
ex.how: Spine and legs only.

ex.title: 8 animals, 90 seconds each
ex.how: Add the rib cage, pelvis and head as masses.

units.title: Animal structure
units.goal: Build animals from simple forms: a rib cage, a pelvis, and the bend of the legs.
look: Many animals walk on their toes
The rib cage is deep and narrow
Leg joints bend in alternating directions

ex.title: 6 animals, 5 minutes each
ex.how: Structure with simple forms.

ex.title: Animals from memory
ex.how: Draw three animals from memory, then check them against the references.

units.title: Animal studies
units.goal: Longer studies from masters of animal drawing.
look: Fur follows the form underneath
Squint to find the big value groups
Keep the gesture alive in long drawings

ex.title: One study, 30 minutes
ex.how: A careful copy.

ex.title: Copy and compare
ex.how: Copy, then check it in Compare.

tracks.name: Environments
tracks.blurb: Landscapes and places: big shapes, depth and atmosphere.

units.title: Big shapes
units.goal: Split a landscape into foreground, middle ground and background before anything else.
look: Three planes, three values
Overlapping shapes create depth
Simplify trees and hills into flat shapes

ex.title: 8 landscapes, 3 minutes each
ex.how: Foreground, middle ground and background as flat shapes.

units.title: Atmosphere
units.goal: Show distance with value and contrast: things fade as they get further away.
look: Darks get lighter in the distance
Contrast is strongest up close
Edges soften with distance

ex.title: 6 landscapes, 5 minutes each
ex.how: Value studies that show depth.

ex.title: One landscape, 30 minutes
ex.how: A value study of one landscape.

units.title: Your own scene
units.goal: Combine perspective, value and composition in a place of your own.
look: Start from a real place, then change it
Decide the light before you draw
Thumbnail before the final drawing

ex.title: 4 places, 5 minutes each
ex.how: Studies of real streets. Uses your Places board.

ex.title: Design a scene
ex.how: Three thumbnails, then a finished drawing of a scene from imagination.
